fields.permitted_stay: Up to 30 days visa-free (30 consecutive calendar days, counted from the day after entry); policy valid until December 31, 2026
fields.application_channel_detail: No application is needed for business visits of up to 30 days under China's unilateral visa-free policy for German ordinary passport holders, valid through 31 December 2026. For stays over 30 days or purposes outside the policy, apply for an M visa at a Chinese Visa Application Service Centre (COVA online form; appointments required).
exceptions: 30-day visa-free entry applies to German ordinary passport holders for business, tourism, visiting relatives and friends, exchange visits, and transit; policy valid until 31 December 2026
Visa-free stay is counted from the day after entry, up to 30 consecutive calendar days
If the stay exceeds 30 days or the visa-free conditions are not met, apply for an M visa via CVASC using the COVA online form
Employment or remunerated work is not permitted under the visa-free business visit
Register with local PSB within 24 hours if staying in private accommodation; hotels register guests automatically
APEC Business Travel Card holders with CHN on the reverse may use dedicated lanes for longer business stays

The policy runs until 31 December 2026; check before travelling after that date
Stay is counted from 00:00 on the day after entry; there is no cap on the number of entries

note: Verified 2026-08-30 against the consolidated Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, which is directly applicable in every Schengen state. Article 4(1): "Nationals of third countries listed in Annex II shall be exempt from the requirement set out in Article 3(1) for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period." JPN appears in Annex II. Six Schengen ministries were checked independently (Italy, Germany, France, Spain, Netherlands, Greece) and agreed without exception. ETIAS is NOT in operation: the European Commission states it is scheduled to start in the last quarter of 2026, and ETIAS applies to visa-free nationals, so it presupposes exemption and never establishes a visa requirement. The Entry/Exit System has been fully operational since 10 April 2026; it is biometric border registration, not a visa and not a travel authorisation. | Corrected 2026-08-30 against the EU's own ETIAS site. Our text named a launch in the last quarter of 2026 and a 7 euro fee. The official page commits to no date, saying only that several months notice will be given, and states the fee as 20 euros. A date we assert that the source does not is a claim of our own.

fields.application_channel_detail: No visa and no travel authorisation are required today. Present a valid passport at the border, where the EU Entry/Exit System registers biometrics.
fields.permitted_stay: 90 days in any 180-day period
exceptions: ETIAS is not in operation and collects no applications. The European Union has not announced a start date and says it will give several months notice before launch. When it starts, the fee will be 20 euros, with applicants under 18 or 70 and over exempt
The Entry/Exit System registers biometrics at the border, fully operational since 10 April 2026; it is not a visa
The 90 days are counted across the whole Schengen area, not per country
Paid employment is not permitted on a visa-free short stay

verified_by: Ellis source audit (Schengen Annex II sweep)
note: Verified 2026-08-30 against the consolidated Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, which is directly applicable in every Schengen state. Article 4(1): "Nationals of third countries listed in Annex II shall be exempt from the requirement set out in Article 3(1) for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period." KOR appears in Annex II. Six Schengen ministries were checked independently (Italy, Germany, France, Spain, Netherlands, Greece) and agreed without exception. ETIAS is NOT in operation: the European Commission states it is scheduled to start in the last quarter of 2026, and ETIAS applies to visa-free nationals, so it presupposes exemption and never establishes a visa requirement. The Entry/Exit System has been fully operational since 10 April 2026; it is biometric border registration, not a visa and not a travel authorisation. | Corrected 2026-08-30 against the EU's own ETIAS site. Our text named a launch in the last quarter of 2026 and a 7 euro fee. The official page commits to no date, saying only that several months notice will be given, and states the fee as 20 euros. A date we assert that the source does not is a claim of our own.

exceptions: ETIAS is not in operation and collects no applications. The European Union has not announced a start date and says it will give several months notice before launch. When it starts, the fee will be 20 euros, with applicants under 18 or 70 and over exempt
The Entry/Exit System registers biometrics at the border, fully operational since 10 April 2026; it is not a visa
The 90 days are counted across the whole Schengen area, not per country
Paid employment is not permitted on a visa-free short stay

verified_by: Ellis source audit (Schengen Annex II sweep)
note: Verified 2026-08-30 against the consolidated Regulation (EU) 2018/1806, which is directly applicable in every Schengen state. Article 4(1): "Nationals of third countries listed in Annex II shall be exempt from the requirement set out in Article 3(1) for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period." SGP appears in Annex II. Six Schengen ministries were checked independently (Italy, Germany, France, Spain, Netherlands, Greece) and agreed without exception. ETIAS is NOT in operation: the European Commission states it is scheduled to start in the last quarter of 2026, and ETIAS applies to visa-free nationals, so it presupposes exemption and never establishes a visa requirement. The Entry/Exit System has been fully operational since 10 April 2026; it is biometric border registration, not a visa and not a travel authorisation. | Corrected 2026-08-30 against the EU's own ETIAS site. Our text named a launch in the last quarter of 2026 and a 7 euro fee. The official page commits to no date, saying only that several months notice will be given, and states the fee as 20 euros. A date we assert that the source does not is a claim of our own.

note: Verified 2026-08-30 against Directive 2004/38/EC on the right of Union citizens to move and reside freely. Article 6(1): "Union citizens shall have the right of residence on the territory of another Member State for a period of up to three months without any conditions or any formalities other than the requirement to hold a valid identity card or passport." This is free movement, not a visa exemption: the Schengen 90/180 rule for third-country nationals does not apply, and a stay beyond three months remains lawful under Article 7 subject to registration in the host state. Confirmed on the Commission's Your Europe guidance.

No financial proof after two previous visits. Two or more trips to Japan in the past three years on a designated individual tourist visa remove the financial documents for the three-year multiple-entry visa; submit the visa notices from those trips and the passports instead.
